concepts.def: Repeated cycle of designing, prototyping and testing that progressively refines a product based on feedback.
Initial statement of the problem and requirements set by a client or identified through research, initiating the design process.
Set of measurable criteria a product must meet, covering function, materials, dimensions, cost and user needs.
Working or appearance model of a design used to test ideas, gather user feedback and refine specifications.
Critical review of a prototype against the specification, identifying improvements for the next iteration.
Information gathered from intended users through interviews, observation or testing, feeding decisions for iteration.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Product Development & Iterative Design — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Product Development & Iterative Design brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Product Development & Iterative Design.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

They are the same thing with different names.
A process used only for software.
CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
